rulings.text: When deleting a sheet for good arrives, every workbook name pointing at that sheet must be removed, so formulas using it give #NAME?, not #REF! as in Excel. Workbook constants and names on other sheets stay.
rulings.test: cp54c ruling: workbook names on the deleted sheet are removed
rulings.deletedFromTrigger:
## Workbook names

- Every workbook name (checkpoint 53) whose target is on the deleted sheet is removed from the
  book. A formula that used it then gives `#NAME?`, unless its own sheet has a name of that name.
  This is NOT what Excel does (Excel keeps the name, pointing at `#REF!`). Workbook constants and
  names on other sheets are kept. Each sheet's own names never point at another sheet and are
  kept.

rulings.text: When undo across a whole workbook arrives, a redone step must count as made at the moment of the redo, not when it was first made, so book.undo() takes it before older steps on other sheets.
rulings.test: cp55c ruling: a redone step counts as made at the time of the redo
rulings.deletedFromTrigger:
- Every step has the time it was made. A step that is redone (by `sheet.redo()` or `book.redo()`)
  counts as made at the time of the redo, and a step that is undone (by either) has the time of that
  undo.
rulings.triggerNowReads:
- Every step has the time it was made, and a step that is undone (by `sheet.undo()` or
  `book.undo()`) has the time of that undo.

rulings.text: When batches arrive, book.batch called while a batch of the same workbook is running must throw #BATCH with cell "batch", never join it. We tried joining, and the inner rollback threw away the outer batch's work.
rulings.test: cp66c ruling: a batch started inside a running batch of the same workbook throws #BATCH
rulings.deletedFromTrigger:
- `book.addSheet`, `book.removeSheet`, `book.renameSheet`, `book.deleteSheet` and `book.batch` throw
  `#BATCH` when called while `fn` runs (`cell` = the method name, such as `"addSheet"`), changing
  nothing. Thrown out of `fn`, that error rolls the batch back like any other. This is NOT what you
  might expect (a nested batch is refused, not joined).
[...]
`batch` checks, in this order, and throws at the first failure, calling nothing:

| Check | `code` | `cell` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no batch of this workbook is running | `#BATCH` | `"batch"` |
| `fn` is a function | `#ARG` | `String(fn)` |
